$\kappa(x)=\dfrac{e^x}{(1+e^{2x})^{3/2}}$. The numerator of $\kappa'$ is $e^x(1+e^{2x})-3e^{3x}=e^x(1-2e^{2x})$, which is zero when $e^{2x}=\frac12$, i.e. $x=-\frac{\ln2}{2}$ ($\kappa'$ changes from $+$ to $-$ there):
\[\boxed{\Big(-\tfrac{\ln2}{2},\ \tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}\Big)}.\]

$\vec r\,'(0)=\langle-2,-1,1\rangle$ and $\vec r\,''=\langle1,2,2\rangle$. Then $\vec r\,'\times\vec r\,''=\langle-4,5,-3\rangle$, with length $\sqrt{50}$:
\[\kappa=\frac{|\vec r\,'\times\vec r\,''|}{|\vec r\,'|^3}=\frac{5\sqrt2}{6\sqrt6}=\boxed{\frac{5\sqrt3}{18}}\approx0.481.\]
